prompt: What does a "white-label" app mean when an agency sells it to a client?

options: An app built entirely from scratch to the client's unique specification
An app that can only be used with a white colour theme
A free open-source app with no support
A ready-built product the agency rebrands and configures for the client, who launches it under their own name
mcq.explanation: White-label means the base product already exists; the client gets their brand, configuration and usually some customisation on top, which is why it is faster and cheaper than a custom build.

prompt: A startup founder wants to launch a food-delivery app in one city within six weeks on a small budget. Why might a white-label solution suit them better than a custom build?

options: White-label apps never need any customisation
White-label apps are owned outright by the agency's other clients
Custom builds cannot include payments
The core flows (ordering, payments, tracking, admin) already exist, so launch is faster and cheaper
mcq.explanation: The value of white-label is time and cost to market for a well-understood model. Some customisation is still normal.

prompt: A prospect loves the white-label demo but lists 14 major changes to how the core marketplace works. What is the most honest advice?

options: Tell them white-label products can never be changed
Ignore the changes and send the standard white-label quote
With that much change to the core, a custom build (possibly reusing parts) may be cheaper and cleaner in the long run; compare both
Promise all 14 changes at the white-label price to win the deal
mcq.explanation: Heavy changes to the core erode white-label's speed and cost advantage and create a fork that is hard to upgrade. Showing both options builds trust and avoids a loss-making deal.

prompt: Which question matters most to qualify a white-label lead before quoting?

options: How many developers do you employ?
Have you ever used an app before?
How does your business model differ from the standard flow the product supports?
What is your favourite app colour?
mcq.explanation: The fit between their model and the product's built-in flows decides whether white-label works and how much customisation it needs.

prompt: Rank these prospects by how well a white-label delivery-app product fits them, best fit first.

task.prompt: Rank these prospects by how well a white-label delivery-app product fits them, best fit first.

items.label: A courier firm needing delivery with a custom multi-stop route optimiser
A biotech lab wanting a sample-tracking system for regulators
A restaurant group launching standard food delivery in two cities next quarter
A grocery startup that wants standard delivery plus its own loyalty points

task.explanation: Closest to the product's standard flows fits best; each step down adds more custom work, and the lab's need is a different product entirely.

prompt: Mark the claims in this white-label sales email that are risky or untrue.

segments.text: Our ready-made delivery platform includes customer, driver and admin apps.

segments.issue: White-label products are licensed to many clients; exclusive ownership needs a different (custom or buy-out) agreement.

prompt: A taxi operator asks for "an app like Uber" for their 40-car fleet, launching in two months, with a modest budget.

task.prompt: A taxi operator asks for "an app like Uber" for their 40-car fleet, launching in two months, with a modest budget.

steps.question: What do you propose first?
options: A full custom build quote
A six-month discovery programme
A demo of the white-label ride-hailing product to check fit against their flows
steps.explanation: Their need is close to a standard model, the timeline is short and budget modest: check white-label fit first.

steps.question: They want drivers paid weekly instead of per ride. How do you treat this?
options: Check whether the product supports configurable payouts; if not, scope it as a priced customisation
Promise it is included without checking
Say it is impossible
steps.explanation: Confirm with the product/engineering team, then price it if it is not standard.

steps.question: They ask whether they can change the product later. What is the right answer?
options: Yes, unlimited changes are free forever
Yes, through scoped customisation, with the trade-off that heavy changes can make upgrades harder
No, white-label can never change
steps.explanation: Honest about flexibility and the upgrade trade-off.

prompt: A client on a white-label plan asks when a custom build would become cheaper overall. Using the numbers below, how many months until the custom option's total cost equals the white-label total?

task.prompt: A client on a white-label plan asks when a custom build would become cheaper overall. Using the numbers below, how many months until the custom option's total cost equals the white-label total?
task.explanation: 15,000 + 2,000m = 60,000 + 500m, so 1,500m = 45,000 and m = 30. Before month 30 white-label is cheaper.

prompt: A reseller (a marketing agency) wants to resell your white-label AI chatbot to their own clients under their brand.

task.prompt: A reseller (a marketing agency) wants to resell your white-label AI chatbot to their own clients under their brand.

steps.question: What is the key commercial question to settle first?
options: The chatbot's default font
Whether they have a LinkedIn page
Pricing structure: per-client licence or revenue share, and who supports end clients
steps.explanation: Reseller deals live or die on margin and support responsibility.

steps.question: They want to promise their clients 100% accurate answers. What do you advise?
options: Not to: AI answers can be wrong; set expectations and include human hand-off or review
Agree, it helps them sell
Tell them to avoid mentioning AI at all
steps.explanation: Overpromising AI accuracy creates support load and churn for both parties.

steps.question: One of their clients needs a custom integration with an in-house ERP. How do you handle it?
options: Refuse all integrations
Scope it as a separate paid customisation through the reseller
Include it free to keep the reseller happy
steps.explanation: Custom integrations are real engineering; price them and keep the reseller as the contracting party.
